question: Your CI pipeline uses Claude Code to generate test cases for pull requests. The test conventions live in .claude/rules/testing.md with the frontmatter paths: ["tests/**/*"]. However, the team keeps each test file next to its component, for example packages/ui/Button.test.tsx and src/checkout/Cart.test.tsx, so the generated tests often ignore the conventions. Which change best fixes this problem?

options.text: Change the paths value to the glob pattern "**/*.test.tsx" so the rule loads for every test file in any directory.
options.reason: Glob patterns in path-specific rules apply conventions by file type regardless of directory location, and the rule still loads only when matching files are edited.

options.text: Move the test conventions into the root CLAUDE.md file so they load in every session, whatever file is edited.
options.reason: The conventions would load even when non-test files are edited, which adds irrelevant context and token usage that path-scoped rules are meant to avoid.

options.text: Copy the test conventions into a CLAUDE.md file in each directory that contains test files.
options.reason: Directory-level CLAUDE.md files are bound to directories, so conventions for files spread across the codebase must be duplicated; glob-pattern rules are the guide's preferred choice for this case.

options.text: Change the paths value to "src/**/*" so the rule loads for every file under the src directory.
options.reason: This pattern is directory-based, so it loads for non-test source files and still misses test files under packages/; it does not target files by type.
